content:
Elena (support): Hey team, NitroSoft reporting frequent SSE streaming truncation when using our Dedicated endpoint through their corporate proxy. They see partial outputs and client attempts to reconnect, which sometimes produces duplicated tokens. Root error timestamp: 2026-02-11T10:12:01Z. thread for triage.

Customer: NitroSoft: Repro is simple, we call chat streaming, after ~28-33s the connection drops and response stops mid-token. Client then reconnects and receives the rest but duplicates last chunk. Not seeing any 4xx/5xx from your side.

Elena (support): Attaching the minimal repro they ran. curl -N test (they used our hosted Dedicated gateway URL):

```bash
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  'https://dedicated.us-east.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-ops-3'
```

Customer: NitroSoft: client logs show: 

```
[10:12:30] GOT: data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...partial token"}}]}
[10:12:31] connection reset by peer
[10:12:31] reconnecting...
[10:12:32] GOT: data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...partial token"}}]}  <-- duplicated chunk
```

Priya (eng-runtime): Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: 1) midstream TCP reset from their corporate proxy/firewall -> partial chunk delivered; client reconnects and server retransmits starting from last acked token so client sees duplication. 2) Path MTU/fragmentation dropping large chunk frames causing partial decodes and connection abort.

Jakob (networking): Curious if their proxy uses HTTP2 termination or strips `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. Also corporate proxies commonly buffer or close idle streams after ~30s. Ask them to confirm proxy vendor/version and any NGINX/HAProxy/GW logs.

Marco (dedicated-oncall): On our side, the Dedicated ingress for that customer runs through a customer-configurable Dedicated LB. I checked our access logs for that window: no 5xx, and the TCP session appears to close with `RST` around the same time. Our runtime emitted these traces: 

```
[runtime] 2026-02-11T10:12:30.987Z stream.write chunk len=1460 seq=782
[runtime] 2026-02-11T10:12:31.001Z socket error: ECONNRESET from peer
```

Marco (dedicated-oncall): ECONNRESET from peer implies client/proxy closed before FIN. Could be MTU or proxy-level connection reuse gone wrong.

Elena (support): Customer says they use a BlueCoat proxy and an on-prem NGINX ingress that does SSL termination + buffering. They specifically called out corporate DLP appliance in the chain.

Priya (eng-runtime): Two actionable routes: 1) Short-term mitigation on our side: send SSE keepalives and smaller chunks so proxies see activity and less chance of large fragmented frames. We can reduce per-chunk size (emit smaller token slices) and include comment keepalives every 10s (`:keepalive\n\n`) which often prevents proxies from timing out. 2) Long-term: recommend customer tunings: disable proxy buffering for the SSE endpoint, enable `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on NGINX, and ensure `proxy_http_version 1.1` and `proxy_set_header Connection ""` or `keep-alive`.

Jakob (networking): Also ask them to check PMTU/path MTU issues. If firewall clamps MSS or drops ICMP, large TLS records can fragment and hit proxy timeouts. Suggest they run `tracepath`/`mturoute` from their egress -> our ingress and check for blackhole. If PMTU blackhole, lowering MTU on their LB (to e.g., 1400) or enabling TCP MSS clamping on the firewall usually fixes it.

Elena (support): I asked customer for: proxy vendor/version, NGINX conf for ingress, tcpdump around the time, and whether they can temporarily disable DLP to test. They provided an NGINX snippet: 

```nginx
server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  proxy_buffering on;  # default
  proxy_read_timeout 60s;
  proxy_send_timeout 60s;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
}
```

Customer: NitroSoft: We can't disable DLP in production but can test on a staging path. We captured a pcap and see many TLS fragments and occasional duplicate retransmits.

Marco (dedicated-oncall): That aligns with PMTU/clamping. Also note `proxy_buffering on` will buffer SSE and may cause early stream termination when buffers fill or proxy times out. Recommend `proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;` and increase `proxy_read_timeout` > 120s.

Priya (eng-runtime): From runtime side, we can implement a small change on the Dedicated gateway for this tenant: 1) enable periodic SSE comments every 10s, 2) limit chunk write size to 512 bytes (instead of 1460) for this customer via a per-tenant override, and 3) add idempotency markers in the SSE stream so clients can dedupe on reconnect (e.g., include a last_delta_id). Are we ok to roll this as a targeted fix?

Aisha (support-lead): Sounds reasonable as an emergency mitigation. We need an RFC for the idempotency marker format but a temporary per-tenant chunk-size override is lower-risk. Priya, can you scope effort?

Priya (eng-runtime): Quick estimate: chunk-size override + keepalive comments = ~2 engineer-days (tests + roll). Idempotency marker + client docs = additional 3-4 days. We can ship the emergency changes behind a tenant flag.

Jakob (networking): For customer-facing steps to unblock them now: 1) set `proxy_buffering off;` 2) add `X-Accel-Buffering: no` header from their ingress (or annotate nginx config) 3) set `proxy_read_timeout` to 180s 4) enable TCP MSS clamping on firewall or set MTU on LB to 1400 for the path to our ingress.

Elena (support): I've told NitroSoft the mitigation list and requested a staging test. They replied: "we tested with `proxy_buffering off` on staging and the stream stayed alive for 8 minutes, no duplicates so far." They will run production change in a maintenance window.

Customer: NitroSoft: We also asked about billing/credits for time lost — they reported an SLA blip. Is that a support escalations policy item?

Aisha (support-lead): Open a billing incident separately; for product-side, confirm whether this counts as SLA breach (we saw a brief drop but no 5xx). Marco, please capture runtime metrics for that window and we can decide on credit.

Marco (dedicated-oncall): Will pull metrics and session traces for 2026-02-11T10:10 -> 10:20.

Priya (eng-runtime): Action items recap: 
- Priya: implement tenant flag for reduced chunk size + periodic SSE keepalive (2d).
- Marco: gather runtime metrics + RST traces for SLA decision.
- Jakob: write a short internal checklist documenting PMTU and proxy signs for streaming truncation.
- Elena: confirm with NitroSoft after their production change and collect pcap if issue persists.
- Aisha: open billing incident for SLA review.

infra-bot: Ticket #INC-4629 created and assigned to eng-runtime.

Elena (support): NitroSoft confirmed maintenance change went in and they've had no further truncations for 48 hours in prod. They will keep us posted. Moving to monitoring; I'll close thread once we have final metrics and billing decision. :thumbsup:

Marco (dedicated-oncall): Got runtime histogram for stream duration; will post baseline + post-fix comparison once done.

Elena (support): Thanks everyone — great cross-team response.
